      "title": "X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is set even when the referer check fails (header set before the raise propagates in some paths)",
      "body": "In `ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = \"ALLOWALL\"` is set AFTER the `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess` guard inside the `if` block, but the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` re-raises a new `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. When the referer is invalid, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false and `raise` executes before the header line — so the header is not set on denial (good). However, the header is set unconditionally for ANY request that passes the referer check, including the `count` action which returns JSON counts for arbitrary embed_urls — this is fine. The actual concern: `ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value (browsers ignore invalid X-Frame-Options values, falling back to default framing protections, but some older/other implementations may treat it permissively). More importantly, setting `ALLOWALL` (rather than removing the header or using CSP frame-ancestors) means any site can frame the content IF the referer check passes — but the referer check is the only gate, and browsers can suppress referers (privacy settings, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`), in which case `request.referer` is nil, `host_allowed?(nil)` returns false, and access is denied — which is safe but breaks legitimate embeds for users with strict referrer policies. This is a known tradeoff; the finding is that the code sets a non-standard header value `ALLOWALL` which is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive (valid values are `DENY` and `SAMEORIGIN`); modern browsers ignore it, so the protection relies entirely on the referer check, and the header provides no real defense. Previously the category came from the global `SiteSetting.embed_category` which always had a value. findings.title: SQL injection in data migration via string interpolation of site setting values
findings.body: The migration builds an INSERT statement by interpolating the raw `embeddable_hosts` site setting value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value comes from the `site_settings` table (previously admin-editable free text, one host per line). Any quote or SQL metacharacter in that setting (e.g. a host line containing `'); DROP TABLE ...;--`) is executed verbatim against the database during `rake db:migrate`. This is a critical SQL injection / data-integrity risk on every deployment that has the old setting populated. Use parameterized queries (`execute` with bind params, or `sanitize_sql_array`, or ActiveRecord inserts) instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: update/destroy crash with NoMethodError when the host id does not exist
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. If the id is missing or stale (e.g. the record was deleted in another tab, or a crafted request), `host` is nil and the request raises `NoMethodError` (500 error) instead of returning a 404. `save_host` also dereferences `host.host = ...` on a possibly-nil object. Add a `raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (or render 404) when the record is not found.

findings.title: Mass-assignment of arbitrary params into EmbeddableHost attributes
findings.body: `save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly from params. While the model only has `host` and `category_id` columns, this pattern bypasses strong-parameter protection and will silently accept and persist any future attribute added to the model (e.g. if a column is later added), and it does not validate that `category_id` refers to an existing category — a bogus category_id is stored, violating referential expectations (the column is `null: false` but there is no FK/validation), leaving orphaned hosts whose category badge renders nothing. Use explicit permitted params and validate the category exists.

findings.title: before_validation mutates nil host, crashing validation when host is blank
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. When `host` is nil (e.g. a create/update request with a missing `embeddable_host[host]` param, which the controller does not guard against), `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, turning a simple validation failure into a 500 error. Guard with `self.host = host.to_s` or `if host.present?` before calling `sub!`, and add a presence validation on `host` (currently only a format validation exists, which is skipped for nil/blank values depending on configuration).

findings.title: Host format regex is too permissive and allows path/port tricks that break referer matching
findings.body: The validation regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` allows an optional port and an arbitrary path suffix (`(\/.*)?`). However `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host` (no port) against the stored value with `lower(host) = ?`. Consequences: (1) a stored host of `example.com:8080` will never match a referer from `example.com` (port stripped by URI parsing), so the admin-configured host silently does not work; (2) a stored host with a path (`example.com/foo`) is stripped by `before_validation` (`self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`) so the path part of the regex is dead code; (3) the regex permits uppercase via `/i` but matching is done with `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host` which is not downcased — `URI('http://EXAMPLE.com').host` returns `EXAMPLE.com` in some Ruby versions, causing a case-sensitivity mismatch and a stored `example.com` failing to match referer `http://EXAMPLE.com/...`. Normalize with `host.downcase` in both the callback and `record_for_host`, and decide whether ports are supported; if not, reject them in validation.

findings.title: Referer host matching is case-sensitive and does not downcase the incoming host
findings.body: `record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host = uri.host`. The stored column is lowered by the DB comparison, but the incoming `uri.host` is NOT downcased. `URI.parse('http://EVILTROUT.COM/x').host` preserves case, so a referer from `http://EVILTROUT.COM` will not match a stored `eviltrout.com`, and conversely the check is inconsistent with the model's own normalization. Downcase the parsed host (`host = uri.host.to_s.downcase`) before the query so matching is deterministic regardless of referer casing.

findings.title: Removing the 'embeddable hosts not set' check changes behavior: embeds are now allowed with zero configured hosts in some paths
findings.body: The old code raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set') if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` before checking the referer. The new code only calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. `host_allowed?` returns `record_for_host(host).present?`, and `record_for_host` returns `false` when the referer is nil/unparseable — so with no hosts configured the behavior is equivalent (denied). However, the explicit 'not set' guard also protected against a nil/blank referer edge case and made the failure mode explicit; more importantly, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (app/models/topic.rb line 869) had its `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` condition removed, so the 'expand embed' UI is now shown whenever any `TopicEmbed` exists for the topic, even if no `EmbeddableHost` rows exist at all — meaning content can be expanded/retrieved for hosts that were never approved. The gating condition should be `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or equivalent) rather than removed entirely.

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host is configured
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to just `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The first condition existed to ensure embedding was enabled (at least one allowed host configured). With it removed, any topic that has a `TopicEmbed` row (e.g. created before hosts were reconfigured, or via feed polling) will show the 'expand embed' affordance even when the site has zero `EmbeddableHost` records, exposing embedded content to visitors on disallowed origins. The check should be replaced with `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or a cached equivalent), not deleted.

findings.title: EmbeddingSerializer embeds only ids but the client expects hydrated host objects with category
findings.body: `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, so the JSON payload contains `embeddable_hosts: [1,2,3]` plus a side-loaded `embeddable_hosts` array. The Ember admin route does `this.store.find('embedding')`, and the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (store.js.es6) maps `embeddable_host_ids` → `embeddable_hosts` only when the payload uses the `_ids` suffix convention with `__rest_serializer: "1"`. The serializer emits `embeddable_hosts` (already plural, ids) rather than `embeddable_host_ids`, so the client-side hydration in `_hydrateEmbedded` (which matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`) will NOT fire for this key, and `embedding.embeddable_hosts` in the controller will be a plain array of integers, not model objects — the `embeddable-host` component's `host.host`, `host.category`, `host.isNew` bindings will all break. Either emit `embeddable_host_ids` with side-loaded objects (matching the rest_serializer convention used elsewhere), or embed objects directly (`embed: :objects`).

findings.title: save() sends buffered 'host' property but the server expects the 'host' attribute inside embeddable_host params
findings.body: In `save()`, `const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host')` fetches the buffered value of the `host` attribute (a string like 'example.com'), then `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and `host.save(props)`. The REST adapter's `update`/`createRecord` wraps attrs as `data['embeddable_host'] = attrs`, so the request body becomes `embeddable_host[host]=example.com&embeddable_host[category_id]=...` — this part is actually correct. However, `getProperties('host')` returns `{host: <string>}` only if the buffered content mixin exposes it that way; if the buffer stores the whole record, `props` could be the record itself and `props.category_id = ...` would mutate the record. More concretely: after a successful save the code does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` but never calls `this.rollbackBuffer()` / `this.set('buffered.host', ...)`, so the buffered (dirty) state persists and `cantSave` (which depends on `buffered.host`) keeps the old value; on the next edit the stale buffer is shown. The buffer must be committed/rolled back after a successful save.

findings.title: edit() reads host.category.id but the serializer only provides category_id, so category is undefined and categoryId becomes undefined
findings.body: `edit()` does `this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`. The `EmbeddableHostSerializer` only emits `id, host, category_id` — there is no embedded `category` object on the client model unless the store hydrates `category_id` into a `category` property. The store's `_hydrateEmbedded` does map `category_id` → `category` via `Discourse.Category.findById(id)` (store.js.es6 `_lookupSubType` special-cases 'category'), but only when the payload is marked `__rest_serializer: "1"` AND the key matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` — the host serializer emits `category_id`, which matches, so hydration may occur. However, the `EmbeddingSerializer` uses `embed: :ids` for hosts, so host objects are side-loaded under an `embeddable_hosts` key; whether each side-loaded host object gets `_hydrateEmbedded` applied depends on the root payload having `__rest_serializer: "1"` (the controller passes `rest_serializer: true`, which should set it). If hydration does not run (e.g. the side-loaded array isn't processed through `_hydrate` with the root), `host.category` is undefined and `this.get('host.category.id')` returns undefined, so `categoryId` is undefined and the category chooser starts blank on edit — the admin cannot see the current category and saving would send `category_id=undefined`, which the server treats as blank and resets to uncategorized. This needs verification/fix: prefer `this.get('host.category_id')` which is always present on the model.

findings.title: addHost pushes a new record into embedding.embeddable_hosts but the array may be a plain JS array of ids, not an Ember array of models
findings.body: Depending on whether the store hydrates the `embeddable_hosts` relationship (see the EmbeddingSerializer finding), `this.get('embedding.embeddable_hosts')` may be a plain array of integer ids rather than an Ember.Array of `embeddable-host` models. `pushObject` is an Ember.Array method; on a plain array it throws `pushObject is not a function`, breaking the 'Add Host' button. Even when it is an Ember array, pushing a `createRecord('embeddable-host')` with no attributes creates a record with `host: undefined`; the component's `cantSave` checks `Ember.isEmpty(host)` on the buffered host string, which is correct, but the new record is immediately rendered in `editing` mode (because `host.isNew` is true) with an empty host input — acceptable — yet if the user cancels, `deleteHost` removes it from the array but the record remains in the store's identity map as a new record; this is minor. The primary risk is the type mismatch of `embeddable_hosts`.

findings.title: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch maps ids but does not handle missing/undefined entries and mutates obj while iterating
findings.body: The new plural branch `obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); })` assumes `obj[k]` is always an array. If a serializer emits `color_ids: null` or omits entries, `obj[k].map` throws. Additionally, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined` (when the id isn't found in the side-loaded collection), producing an array full of `undefined` holes assigned to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` — downstream code doing `colors[0].get('id')` (as the new store test does) will crash. The singular branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch does not filter out unresolved ids. Filter out falsy results: `obj[k].map(...).filter(function(x){ return !!x; })` or similar, and guard `if (!obj[k]) { return; }`.

findings.title: basePath type normalization only replaces the first underscore, breaking multi-word admin model types
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` (without a global flag) replaces only the FIRST underscore. The `ADMIN_MODELS` list contains `'embeddable-host'` (single word, fine), but any future admin model with two underscores (e.g. `site_customization_field` → expected `site-customization-field`) would only become `site-customization_field` and fail the `indexOf` check, silently routing an admin model's requests to the non-admin base path `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` for correctness and robustness.

findings.title: Category fabricators were moved into the wrong file: category_fabricator.rb now defines the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines categories
findings.body: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was overwritten to contain ONLY the `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` block, deleting the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. Meanwhile `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` (new file) contains the category fabricators. The file names are swapped relative to their contents: every spec that does `Fabricate(:category)` relies on the category fabricators being loaded (Fabrication auto-loads all files under spec/fabricators, so loading may still work), but this is a serious maintainability/correctness defect — the file named `category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines a `:category` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` does not define `:embeddable_host`. Any tooling, generator, or developer that expects fabricators to live in the file matching their name (and any `require` of a specific fabricator file) breaks. The contents of the two files must be swapped back so each file defines the fabricator matching its name.

findings.title: update action is a no-op that just re-renders, giving a false sense that embedding settings can be saved
findings.body: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or persisting any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and the admin controller's `saveChanges` action (`this.get('embedding').update({})`) both target it. Since hosts are created/updated/deleted through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, the embedding `update` endpoint is misleading dead code: a client PUTing embedding-level settings (if any are ever added) would silently succeed without persisting anything. Either implement it to accept and persist embedding-level attributes, or remove the route/action to avoid a misleading API surface.

findings.title: Authorization relies on redundant before_filter in addition to route constraint; ensure_staff allows moderators, route allows only admins — verify intended privilege level
findings.body: The routes declare `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (admin-only), but the controller adds `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` (staff = admins + moderators). The effective access is the intersection (admin-only via route), so moderators get 404 rather than 403. This is not a vulnerability per se, but the controller's `ensure_staff` is misleading dead weight and inconsistent with sibling admin controllers that rely on the route constraint alone (e.g. `Admin::EmbeddingController` uses `ensure_staff` too but its routes also use `AdminConstraint`). More importantly, the `create`/`update`/`destroy` actions mutate which external sites can embed and iframe forum content (a security-sensitive setting affecting X-Frame-Options / referer allowlisting); confirm admin-only is intended and remove the redundant/misleading `ensure_staff` filter, or document why moderators are filtered at the controller level but blocked at the route level.

findings.title: Serializer defines trivial attribute methods that just delegate to the object; also missing category object for the client
findings.body: The explicit `def id; object.id; end` etc. methods are redundant — `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` already generates them. More importantly, the admin UI (`embeddable-host.hbs`) renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`, which requires a `category` object on the client model, but the serializer only emits `category_id`. The client store can hydrate `category_id` → `category` via `Discourse.Category.findById` only when the payload is processed as a rest_serializer payload with the root containing categories; the `EmbeddingSerializer` side-loads hosts but does not include a `categories` array, so `Discourse.Category.findById` may return undefined if categories aren't already loaded in the client. The serializer should either embed the category (`has_one :category` / `embed: :objects`) or the embedding payload should side-load categories, otherwise the category badge column renders blank.

findings.title: Controller specs only assert inheritance; no tests for create/update/destroy behavior, authorization, or validation errors
findings.body: Both new controller specs (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController`) contain a single test asserting the class is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests covering: successful host creation/update/destroy, rejection of non-staff users, handling of missing/invalid host params (which currently 500 due to the nil-host bug in the model), the nil-record 404 path in update/destroy, or the embedding show/update serialization shape. Given these endpoints mutate security-sensitive embed allowlisting, the test coverage is inadequate — the existing bugs (nil host crash, missing record crash) would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for blank/nil host (which crashes before_validation) and no test for case-insensitive referer matching
findings.body: The spec covers trimming http/https/paths and `host_allowed?` for exact hosts, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil).valid?` — which currently raises `NoMethodError` on `nil.sub!` in `before_validation` (the bug noted in the model finding); (2) case-insensitive matching (`host_allowed?('http://EVILTROUT.COM')` vs stored `eviltrout.com`) — which the current `record_for_host` implementation gets wrong because it doesn't downcase `uri.host`; (3) uniqueness — two hosts differing only by case (`Example.com` vs `example.com`) can both be saved because there is no uniqueness validation, and `lower(host) = ?` matching means they are duplicates functionally. Add a uniqueness validation (scoped with `lower`) and tests for these cases.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host — duplicate/case-variant hosts can be created
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost` validates only the format of `host`. There is no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive). Because `record_for_host` matches with `lower(host) = ?`, storing both `Example.com` and `example.com` creates functionally duplicate rows that both match the same referers; the admin UI will show two rows for the same site, and deleting one still leaves embedding enabled. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false` (and ideally a unique index in the migration) to prevent duplicate allowlist entries.

findings.title: Migration lacks a unique index on host and does not downcase migrated values
findings.body: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but no unique index. Since `record_for_host` matches case-insensitively (`lower(host) = ?`), duplicate rows (including case variants) will silently coexist and all match — there is no DB-level guard. Also, the migrated values from the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting are inserted verbatim (`'#{h}'`) without stripping `http://` prefixes or paths (the model's `before_validation` normalization is bypassed because raw SQL INSERT is used), so a legacy value like `http://example.com/path` becomes a stored host of `http://example.com/path`, which will never match a referer (referer matching compares only `uri.host`). The migration should normalize each host (strip scheme/path, downcase) before insert and add a unique index on `lower(host)`.

findings.title: Blank category_id silently falls back to uncategorized, masking client errors
findings.body: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` silently converts a missing/invalid category selection into the uncategorized category. If the admin UI sends `category_id` as an empty string (e.g. the category chooser not initialized — see the `edit()` finding where `categoryId` can be undefined), the host is saved pointing at uncategorized without any error, so embedded posts land in the wrong category with no feedback. This should either be a validation error when `category_id` is blank on create, or at minimum the fallback should only apply when the param is absent, not when it's an invalid/nonexistent id. Also, `uncategorized_category_id` is typically a negative sentinel (-1) that may not correspond to a real Category row, so `belongs_to :category` will be nil and the badge renders blank.

findings.title: Table is only rendered when embeddable_hosts is non-empty, so a new host cannot be added when the list is empty
findings.body: `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` wraps the entire `<table>` including the `{{embeddable-host}}` rows. When there are zero hosts, the table (and its header row) is not rendered at all — only the 'Add Host' button shows. When the admin clicks 'Add Host', `addHost` pushes a new record into `embedding.embeddable_hosts`, which makes the `{{#if}}` become true and the table appears — so functionally it works. However, the `{{#each}}` over a possibly plain array (see controller finding) and the conditional table mean the header only appears after the first add; more importantly, if `embeddable_hosts` is a plain array of ids (not models), `{{#if}}` is truthy for `[1,2]` but `{{embeddable-host host=host}}` receives an integer, breaking rendering. The template should render the table header unconditionally and iterate safely.

findings.title: @on('didInsertElement') combined with @observes('editing') refocuses the input on every edit toggle and on insert, stealing focus unexpectedly
findings.body: The `_focusOnInput` method is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The observer fires whenever `editing` changes (becoming true when entering edit mode, and again when leaving), and `didInsertElement` fires on render. When `editing` becomes false after save/cancel, the observer still runs and schedules `this.$('.host-name').focus()` — but by then the input is gone (the `{{#if editing}}` block rendered the read-only view), so `this.$('.host-name')` is empty and focus is lost (or, in a race, focus may be applied to a removed element). This causes the page focus to jump to the body after saving. The `@observes('editing')` should be guarded to only focus when entering edit mode (`if (this.get('editing'))`), or the observer should be removed in favor of focusing only on `didInsertElement` when `isNew`.

findings.title: Locale string 'Allowed Hosts' is used as a table column header for a single host value, and 'Post to Category' is ambiguous
findings.body: The new `admin.embedding` locale block defines `host: "Allowed Hosts"` (plural) which is used in `embedding.hbs` as the column header for an individual host value (`{{i18n "admin.embedding.host"}}` above a column of single hostnames). A column listing individual hosts should be labeled "Host" or "Allowed Host", not "Allowed Hosts". Similarly `category: "Post to Category"` describes the category that embedded topics are posted into — it is used as a column header for the category badge, so "Category" would be clearer. These are user-facing admin strings; the plural/ambiguous wording will confuse admins managing the allowlist.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is set even when the referer check fails (header set before the raise propagates in some paths)
findings.body: In `ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is set AFTER the `raise Discourse::InvalidAccess` guard inside the `if` block, but the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` re-raises a new `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. When the referer is invalid, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` returns false and `raise` executes before the header line — so the header is not set on denial (good). However, the header is set unconditionally for ANY request that passes the referer check, including the `count` action which returns JSON counts for arbitrary embed_urls — this is fine. The actual concern: `ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value (browsers ignore invalid X-Frame-Options values, falling back to default framing protections, but some older/other implementations may treat it permissively). More importantly, setting `ALLOWALL` (rather than removing the header or using CSP frame-ancestors) means any site can frame the content IF the referer check passes — but the referer check is the only gate, and browsers can suppress referers (privacy settings, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`), in which case `request.referer` is nil, `host_allowed?(nil)` returns false, and access is denied — which is safe but breaks legitimate embeds for users with strict referrer policies. This is a known tradeoff; the finding is that the code sets a non-standard header value `ALLOWALL` which is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive (valid values are `DENY` and `SAMEORIGIN`); modern browsers ignore it, so the protection relies entirely on the referer check, and the header provides no real defense. Consider using CSP `frame-ancestors` with the allowlisted hosts instead.

findings.title: Embedded topic category now comes from EmbeddableHost, but when no host matches, category is nil and PostCreator may create an uncategorized topic or fail
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` now does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator`. When the URL's host is not in the allowlist (which can happen because `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` gates retrieval, but `TopicEmbed.import` is also called directly from feed polling `Jobs::PollFeed` and potentially other paths that may not check the allowlist first), `eh` is nil/false and `category` is nil. `PostCreator` with a nil category will create a topic in the uncategorized category (or fail validation if `allow_uncategorized_topics` is false and the user is not staff). Previously the category came from the global `SiteSetting.embed_category` which always had a value. The behavior change means feed-polled or directly-imported embeds without a matching host silently land in uncategorized (or error). The import path should either skip import when no host matches (return nil) or fall back to a configured default category, and this should be tested.

findings.title: invalid_host? now depends on EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? which returns false for nil referer, but the retriever is initialized with an embed_url, not a referer — semantics changed
findings.body: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(@embed_url)`. `host_allowed?` → `record_for_host(host)` does `URI(host)` and extracts `uri.host`. The `@embed_url` is the URL of the external page being embedded (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/2013/02/10/why-discourse-uses-emberjs.html`), so `uri.host` is `eviltrout.com` — this is correct and matches the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` behavior. However, `record_for_host` returns `false` (not nil) when URI parsing fails, and `host_allowed?` returns `record_for_host(host).present?` → `false.present?` → `false`, so `invalid_host?` returns `!false` = `true` — correct. The semantics are preserved. The only concern is that `record_for_host` returns `false` or a record, and `.present?` on `false` is `false` — fine. No bug here; this finding is withdrawn as it is a restatement. (Not reporting.)
